data.title: Crown Castle jumps 16% amid heavy trading, sector gains
data.description:
Shares of Crown Castle Inc. (CCI), a U.S.-focused telecommunications infrastructure REIT, rallied almost 16% on Friday, as volume surged to more than three times its one-month average daily pace.

The broader real estate sector also moved higher today, with the XLRE sector ETF gaining just under 2%, and tower REIT peers American Tower and SBA Communications rose just over 9% and just over 7%, respectively.

What Happened to Crown Castle

Telecom tower REIT stocks got a major boost after investment firm Grain Management said SpaceX (SPCX) is set to acquire 100% of its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio.

Crown Castle is a pure-play U.S. tower REIT following its strategic decision to divest its Fiber and Small Cell businesses. Its largest tenants are T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon Wireless, who together represented approximately 90% of 2025 site-rental revenue, according to the company's SEC filing.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count jumps by 5 in Baker Hughes survey
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. gained 5 to 603, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. jumped by 6 to 462 in the week ended October 2, while gas rigs dropped by 1 to 132 and miscellaneous rigs remained unchanged at 9.

The total rig count was up by 56, or 10.2%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 44, or 10.5%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 12, or 10%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin rose by 4 in the past week to 273, while the Eagle Ford and Williston Basin counts totaled 41 and 30, respectively, flat compared to the previous week.

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Monday
data.description:
Wall Street regained some momentum on Friday, after the AI trade came under pressure on Thursday.

S&P 500 (SP500) +0.6%, the Dow (DJI) +0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.6%.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Monday:

  • The six-day Paris Auto Show will begin. The press conference and model announcement schedule will feature mostly European automakers, although appearances by Tesla's (TSLA) Cybercab and Chinese automakers BYD (BYDDF), Changan, Chery, Geely, XPeng (XPEV), Li Auto (LI), and Leapmotor give the auto show a more global feel this year.
  • Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack will give the keynote at the 68th NABE Annual Meeting in Cleveland. The theme is "Global Structural Reset: AI, Demographics, and Geopolitics."
  • U.S. stock exchanges will be fully operational, but the cash Treasury market is officially closed for Columbus Day/Indigenous Peoples' Day.

data.title: FDA issues alert on Philips Lumify ultrasound following reports of deaths, injuries
data.description:
• The US FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health has issued an Early Alert regarding Philips' (PHG) Lumify Diagnostic Ultrasound System due to a software issue that has prevented scanning functionality. 
  • As a result, there have been delays in diagnosis or treatment that has led to reports of four deaths and eight serious injuries, as of Sept. 29.
  • The "Lumify Android or iOS application used with its ultrasound transducers may not recognize a previously registered transducer and will prompt users for re-registration without warning prior to point-of-care use," the alert states. "Scanning functionality is prevented until the registration step has been completed.
  • Philips Ultrasound sent out letters on Sept. 24 regarding the issue, advising healthcare professionals that use Lumify to have readily accessible Wi-FI/cellular signals, unless a backup device is immediately available, and to always have backup ultrasound devices. 
  • The company is also developing a software update and determining the cause of the issue.

data.title: Alpine Income Property expands with $117.3M industrial property deal
data.description:
• Alpine Income Property Trust (PINE) announced on Friday that it agreed to acquire a 13-property industrial portfolio for $117.3M, or $63 per square foot.
  • The portfolio spans 1.9M square feet across 11 states and is fully leased to nine tenants, with a weighted average remaining lease term of 10.2 years. 
  • No leases expire before late 2031.
  • About 19% of in-place cash rent comes from investment-grade tenants or subsidiaries of investment-grade parents. 
  • The acquisition is expected to close in Q4 2026 and will be fully funded through revolving credit borrowings, property sale proceeds, and commercial loan repayments.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Accendra Health receives NYSE notice
data.description:
• Accendra Health (ACH)  said on Friday it received a notice from the NYSE after its average closing share price fell below $1 for 30 consecutive trading days.
  • The company plans to notify the NYSE of its intent to cure the deficiency within 10 business days and has six months to regain compliance.
  • Accendra Health is considering options, including a reverse stock split subject to shareholder approval at its next annual meeting, expected in May 2027.
  • The company shares will continue trading on the NYSE during the six-month compliance period, subject to meeting other listing standards.
  • Share -3.43%

data.description:

data.title: DuPont, Illinois Tool Works cut to Neutral at J.P. Morgan on downside short-cycle trends
data.description:
DuPont (DD) and Illinois Tool Works (ITW) were downgraded Friday to Neutral from Overweight with $145 and $277 price target, cut from $172 and $300, at J.P. Morgan, which cited concerns over decelerating short-cycle industrial demand into 2027.

"We are in a 'mid-cycle' stage of the industrial cycle - no longer 'early' - as many B2B/industrial end-market up-cycles are quite mature, and the AI up-cycle is entering year 4, [which] coupled with valuations which are not cheap vs. bond yields, caps the degree to which [electrical equipment and multi-industry sector] multiples can re-rate on a relative basis," JPM's Julian Mitchell said in a note.

The analyst said he has a "mildly positive" view of the EE/MI sector with scope for a "catch-up bounce" given the group's recent stock underperformance and likely positive estimate revisionmomentum at Q3 earnings.

JPM said its thesis on DuPont (DD) "primed for a short-cycle recovery with consistent execution" has largely played out, and while seeing improving trends for some pockets of the company's portfolio, "overall we see organic growth deceleration" into 2027 following above company average organic growth in 2026.

On Illinois Tool Works (ITW), Mitchell said he does "not view the overall short-cycle industrial complex particularly favorably, as we think manufacturing PMIs may not show much further improvement from current levels," meaning little opportunity for positive estimate revision at the company and a fair current valuation for the stock.

Additionally, JPM started Trane (TT) Trane at Overweight as "a best-in-class HVAC name, and we expect it to continue to thrive relative to the group and other HVAC pure-play names," and Carrier Global (CARR) at Neutral as "valuation looks somewhat cheap, but there is considerable uncertainty over the earnings outlook."

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway advances for seven consecutive sessions
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) shares clocked seven straight sessions of gains, as the stock was up 0.9% at $515.45 on Friday.

The holding company gained over 2% in the preceding six sessions. 

Recently, Berkshire Hathaway purchased $53.9M of Lennar (LEN) shares in the last three days of September, pushing the insurance conglomerate's ownership to a stake valued at ~$2.16B. 

Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, BRK has a Hold rating with a score of 3.48 out of 5. The company received A+ in the prospect of profitability, while it received D+ in growth factor.

Seeking Alpha analysts are positive and see the stock as a Buy.

"BRK.B's traditional passive allocation strategy is increasingly at risk, with real returns on T-bills eroded by inflation and limited acquisition targets that meet strict criteria. Strategic pivot toward large-scale energy infrastructure—especially nuclear and geothermal—could unlock long-term value, leveraging Berkshire’s unique capital structure and operating assets," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis report.
